title: Real-part bound for a unit-twisted lift
statement:
Let $k \ge 2$ and let $f : \bbz_k^n \to \bbz_k$ be normalized and $\varepsilon$-far from linear, meaning that $f(0) = 0$, that $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$, and that $\dist(f,g) \ge \varepsilon$ for every linear $g : \bbz_k^n \to \bbz_k$ (where $\dist$ is the fraction of inputs on which two functions disagree). Fix a unit $j \in (\bbz/k\bbz)^\times$ and a frequency $s \in \bbz_k^n$, and let $\widetilde{f}_j(x) = \omega_k^{\,j\,f(x)}$ be the corresponding $j$-twisted lift, with $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$. Then the Fourier coefficient of $\widetilde{f}_j$ at $s$ has real part bounded by
\[
  \operatorname{Re}\,\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s) \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\,\varepsilon .
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is ε-far from every linear function
j is a unit in Z/kZ
s is an arbitrary frequency in Z_k^n
replaced:
If $k \ge 2$, $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far from linear (normalized), $j \in
\mathbb{Z}_k^\times$, and $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$, then
\[
  \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\widehat{(\widetilde{f}_j)}(s)\right]
  \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1-\cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\varepsilon.
\]
